title: A running resident keeps its route code; index.html is read fresh
body:
Verify a route or handler change against a restarted resident: pipe a session-start payload into node hooks/run.cjs session-start, then check GET /api/resident shows stale:false. index.html is read on every GET / and needs only a browser refresh. A resident whose src/ changed refuses hooks (409 build_stale) and is replaced at the next prompt or session start, but until then it keeps serving UI routes with its old code.

Why: A new route returned 404 against the already-running process while a fresh one served it. Stale detection only guards hook calls, so UI routes silently run old code until replacement.

evidence.summary: staleCode() gates /api/hooks/* only; index.html is read per request.
The prompt path now calls ensureResident, which replaces a stale resident.

v1.trigger: when editing src/ui/server.js routes or handlers and verifying against a running audit UI
